entries.topicDescription: Trailing closures, capture semantics, and escaping vs non-escaping closures.

questions.questionText: What is a trailing closure in Swift?
questions.explanation: When a closure is the last argument to a function, it can be written outside the parentheses for cleaner syntax.

answers.answerText: A closure written outside the parentheses when it's the last argument
A closure that runs after the function returns
A closure with no parameters
A closure stored as a global variable

questions.questionText: What does marking a closure parameter '@escaping' mean?
questions.explanation: An escaping closure can outlive the function call it was passed to — e.g. stored in a property or called later on a background queue — instead of being used only within the function's own execution.

answers.answerText: The closure may be called after the function it was passed to has returned
The closure cannot capture any external variables
The closure runs on a background thread automatically
The closure is guaranteed to run exactly once

entries.topicDescription: Associated values, switch exhaustiveness, and if/guard-case pattern matching.

questions.questionText: What are 'associated values' on a Swift enum case?
questions.explanation: A case can carry extra data of its own type, distinct from other cases — e.g. 'case success(String)' vs 'case failure(Error)' — letting an enum model a value plus the data relevant to that specific state.

answers.answerText: Extra data a specific enum case carries along with it
A default value assigned to every case
A computed property shared by all cases
A protocol every case must conform to

questions.questionText: Why must a 'switch' statement over a Swift enum be exhaustive?
questions.explanation: The compiler requires every case to be handled (or a 'default') so that adding a new enum case later causes a compile error everywhere it isn't handled, instead of a silent runtime gap.

answers.answerText: So the compiler catches unhandled cases at compile time, not runtime
Because Swift enums cannot have a default case
Because switch statements run faster when exhaustive
It's only a style convention, not enforced by the compiler

entries.topicDescription: Representing the absence of a value safely, without null-pointer crashes.

questions.questionText: What does the '??' nil-coalescing operator do?
questions.explanation: 'a ?? b' returns a if it's non-nil, otherwise evaluates and returns b — a concise way to supply a default value for an optional.

answers.answerText: Returns the left value if non-nil, otherwise the right value
Force-unwraps an optional, crashing if it's nil
Compares two optionals for equality
Converts a non-optional value into an optional

questions.explanation: Writing a?.b?.c safely accesses a chain of optional properties/methods — if any link in the chain is nil, the whole expression short-circuits to nil instead of crashing.

answers.answerText: Safely accessing a chain of optional properties, short-circuiting to nil if any link is nil
Force-unwrapping every optional in an expression at once
Linking multiple optionals into a single array
A way to declare multiple optional variables in one line

entries.topicDescription: Protocol-oriented programming, conformance, and protocol extensions.

questions.questionText: What is a protocol in Swift?
questions.explanation: A protocol defines a blueprint of methods, properties, and requirements that a conforming type must implement.

answers.answerText: A blueprint of methods and properties a type must implement
A concrete base class for inheritance
A networking layer specification
An enum with associated values

questions.questionText: What does a protocol extension with a default implementation let you do?
questions.explanation: A protocol extension can provide a default method body, so conforming types get that behavior for free and only need to override it if they need different behavior — the core of Swift's protocol-oriented programming style.

answers.answerText: Give conforming types a default behavior they don't have to implement themselves
Force every conforming type to override every method
Turn the protocol into a concrete class
Restrict conformance to reference types only

entries.topicDescription: Modern async/await and task-based concurrency in Swift.

questions.questionText: What keyword marks a function as asynchronous in Swift?
questions.explanation: The 'async' keyword marks a function as asynchronous, and 'await' is used at the call site to suspend until the result is ready.

answers.answerText: async
await
suspend
concurrent

questions.questionText: What is an actor in Swift concurrency?
questions.explanation: An actor is a reference type that protects its mutable state from data races by ensuring only one task accesses its state at a time.

answers.answerText: A type that isolates mutable state to prevent data races
A class that runs on the main thread only
A protocol for networking
A design pattern for dependency injection
